questions.question: In a row of 205 students, A is sitting 56th from the left end and B is sitting 112th from the right end. If A and B interchange their seats, then what will be the new position of A from the left end?
questions.questionHtml: In a row of 205 students, A is sitting 56th from the left end and B is sitting 112th from the right end. If A and B interchange their seats, then what will be the new position of A from the left end?
questions.solution:
Total students = 205
B is 112th from the right end.

B’s position from the left end = Total - Right position + 1
= 205 - 112 + 1
= 94th

After interchanging seats, A will sit at B’s original position.
So, the new position of A from the left end = 94th.

You have to assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the suggested courses of action logically follow(s) for pursuing. Statement: A large number of road accidents are being reported due to overspeeding in the city. Course of action I: Ban all vehicles in the city immediately. questions.questionHtml:
In each question below is given a statement followed by two courses of action numbered I and II. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the suggested courses of action logically follow(s) for pursuing.

Statement: A large number of road accidents are being reported due to overspeeding in the city.

Course of action I: Ban all vehicles in the city immediately.
Course of action II: Implement stricter traffic rules and run awareness campaigns for drivers.
questions.solution:
Course of action I is too extreme and not practical; banning all vehicles is not a reasonable solution.

Course of action II is logical, as stricter traffic rules and awareness campaigns will reduce overspeeding and accidents.

Hence, only Course of action II should be followed.

questions.question: If February 29, 2032, falls on a Sunday, what day of the week will February 29, 2036, be?
questions.questionHtml: If February 29, 2032, falls on a Sunday, what day of the week will February 29, 2036, be?
questions.solution:
29 Feb 2032 → Sunday

28 Feb 2033 → 1 odd day (365 days → 1 day forward)

28 Feb 2034 → 1 odd day

28 Feb 2035 → 1 odd day

29 Feb 2036 → 2 odd days (leap year adds 2)

Total odd days = 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 5 days

Sunday + 5 days = Friday
